title: No ancient bishop painted Christ or the saints
english: Which of the ancient bishops dishonored Christ by painting him? Which of them made a public example of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, of Moses and the prophets, of Peter or Andrew or James or John or the rest of the apostles, and paraded them in triumph in this way? At the same time they are lying, fashioning forms of the saints from their own thought in different ways—sometimes making the same ones old men, sometimes younger—entering into things they have never seen. They paint the Savior with long hair based on conjecture, because he is called a Nazarene, since Nazirites have long hair. But those who try to connect the types to him go astray, for the Savior drank wine, which Nazirites did not drink. It is not fitting for us to have God painted in colors and limbs.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Epistula ad Theodosium imperatorem u01-rem-early
orientation: Epiphanius is asking the emperor whether any ancient bishop ever painted Christ or the saints, and is beginning to explain why painters who do so are inventing false appearances.

title: Painters invent false appearances of Peter, Paul, and the disciples
english: For the very thing they fashion from their own thought, they are lying about. The deceivers paint the holy apostle Peter as an old man, with his head and beard shorn. They also paint Saint Paul—some as bald in front, others as bald with a beard—and the other disciples as simply shorn. If the Savior had long hair while the other disciples were shorn, and he was not shorn yet appeared the same as them, then why were the Pharisees and scribes giving thirty pieces of silver to Judas for payment, so that after kissing him he might point out to them, “This is the one you are looking for”? Could they not have found him by themselves or through others, by the sign of the long hair, without giving a reward?
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Epistula ad Theodosium imperatorem u01-rem-mid
orientation: Epiphanius is arguing that painters fabricate the appearances of the saints from their own imagination, and he now gives specific examples of how they depict Peter, Paul, and the other disciples.

title: Epiphanius's requests were mocked and ignored
english: He admits that at first his words were set before the many as mockery, on account of the nonsense he babbled, and then that when he advised his fellow bishops and fellow ministers to have these images removed, he was not listened to. We found at the end of the letter an indication containing this: that after speaking many times to my fellow ministers about removing the images, I was not heeded by them, nor did they endure to hear my voice even for a little.
He asks that the curtains bearing such painting be gathered and go forward for the burial of the poor, and that the paintings on the walls be whitewashed.

As for the images already painted in the shrine, since such a removal is difficult, if it is possible to remove them, that is good; but if it is impossible, to be content with what has already happened and no longer to paint anyone in this way.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Epistula ad Theodosium imperatorem u01-rem-close
orientation: Epiphanius is closing his letter by reporting how his advice to remove images was received and restating his final requests about the curtains, wall paintings, and shrine images.
